A_stable_normal: Covered by the 75-station Stage 1 VALIDATION split — each station's own AR(1) slow/fast components represent stable, low-variance normal behavior.
B_diurnal_variation: Covered inherently — Stage 1's generator embeds a diurnal sinusoid per station.
C_gradual_variation: Covered inherently — the AR(1) slow component represents gradual drift-free variation.
D_long_running_stream: See Stage 6 long-run results (stage6_results/stage6_long_run.json): 5 stations x 5 days x 144/day = 720 steps/station.

max_continuous_elevated_run_investigatio.finding: The 864-step (full-length) elevated run belongs to exactly ONE station, ATHER-BGW-0215,
median integrated score 0.952 across its whole evaluable window. Investigated further:
only 2 of 75 val stations (ATHER-BGW-0215, ATHER-NAM-0110) have a MEDIAN score > 0.70
(i.e. are persistently, not just occasionally, elevated). Both are exactly the two
audit as heavily RH-clipped during synthetic generation -- their humidity trajectory is
erratic/clipped rather than smooth AR(1), so the shared LSTM (trained on the overall
distribution) produces large, persistent residuals against them. This is a SYNTHETIC-DATA
GENERATION limitation already documented in Stage 1.5, not a Temporal Intelligence code
defect -- the layer is correctly reporting a large, real deviation from its learned normal
pattern for these two specific stations.
max_continuous_elevated_run_investigatio.conclusion: Not a new correctness problem -- traced to a previously-documented data limitation affecting a small, identifiable, known subset of stations.

note: These figures are IDENTICAL to Stage 5/6's already-documented results (median~0.354, P95~0.919, 9.6% >0.70, 21.2% reason-rate) -- reported honestly as known limitations, not changed here (validation-only task).
